response.justification: The candidate has genuine geospatial domain experience (founder of an open-source GIS platform) and some low-level systems background (D language, async I/O, fibers, C/C++ at National Instruments), but his C++ exposure is dated (2014-2015) and his most recent five-plus years have been almost entirely TypeScript/Node.js full-stack work with no Rust experience at all. The core required skill—modern C++ or Rust for a routing/tiling pipeline—is not demonstrated in his recent work history, making him a risky fit despite his strong generalist and geospatial background.
strengths: Hands-on geospatial platform development (GISCollective, Green Map GIS app) directly relevant to routing/mapping domain
Past experience with low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems (Dunnhumby: async I/O, fibers, microservices at scale)
Demonstrated versatility across many languages/stacks and strong learning agility (explicit fit for 'willingness to expand expertise')
concerns: No recent (last 5+ years) hands-on C++ or Rust development; skills list omits both entirely
No direct experience with navigation guidance systems or routing tile pipelines
Recent career trajectory (Optilyz, re:cinq) is squarely web/full-stack (TypeScript/Node), a significant pivot away from systems-level programming required for this role
